newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks mixed in morning, property concerns weigh.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks mixed in morning, property concerns weigh.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks traded mixed in Tuesday morning trade, with blue chips meandering around Monday's closing levels as concerns about government measures in the property market limited gains but red chips pushing ahead.
The Hang Seng Index was down 6.01 points, or 0.04 percent, at 14,388.59 after surging 282.05 points on Monday. Turnover was HK$4.07 billion after the first hour minutes of trade.

"Investors are still waiting to see what the government will do about the property market so there is going to be a cap to the upside of the market," said Kent Rossiter, institutional sales manager at Nikko Securities.
"Sideways trading is what we expect given the lack of market moving information from the U.S. market," he added.
The Dow industrials fell 9.95 points to 7,772.09 on Monday.

Red chips retained a firm tone with the new China-Affiliated Corporations Index advancing 37.91 points, or 1.32 percent, to 2,905.23 as investors followed through on Monday's strong momentum. The index gained 7.28 percent on its launch day on Monday.

Percy-Au-Young, director of research at DBS Securities, said the Hang Seng Index was likely to see some resistance at 14,500 points in the short-term due to concerns that Hong Kong's new government will impose measures to rein in spiralling property prices soon after Hong Kong returns to Chinese rule on July 1.
"I don't think it will be easy for the market to go back up to 15,000 in the near future because of the concerns about the residential property market," he said.
Rossiter saw a range of about 14,000 to 15,000 points in the run-up to Hong Kong's change in sovereignty. "I don't see it breaking much above 15,000," he said.
Among the blue chips, some utilities continued to push ahead after leading the market on Monday.
China Light & Power gained HK$0.70 to HK$44.00 and Hongkong Electric was up HK$1.00 at HK$31.90.

Among the property developers, Cheung Kong shed its initial losses to trade up HK$0.75 at HK$74.50 after falling to HK$73.25 earlier. New World Development gained HK$0.30 to HK$46.30 but Sun Hung Kai Properties fell HK$0.50 to HK$87.75.
